title: Where The Years Go
voice_standard: Liam - warm nostalgic, then energized: the friend giving your years back

scenes.text: Be honest with me. Didn't this year feel... short?
scenes.semantic_anchor: Calendar pages blown through: the year that vanished.
scenes.query: calendar pages flipping fast wind time lapse

scenes.text: And not just this one. They're accelerating. Every year, a little faster than the last.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Light trails accelerating: years picking up speed.
scenes.query: highway light trails at night speeding long exposure

scenes.text: Meanwhile, one summer when you were nine lasted approximately... forever.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The endless golden summer of age nine.
scenes.query: children playing in golden field summer evening vintage

scenes.text: Same clocks. Same 365 days. So which one of you is wrong?
scenes.semantic_anchor: A wall of agreeing clocks and disagreeing lifetimes.
scenes.query: many clocks on wall different times ticking

scenes.text: Neither. Because you don't experience time. You experience the RECORDING of time.
scenes.semantic_anchor: PREMIUM GRAPHIC: an elegant amber hourglass where every falling grain is a tiny glowing photograph.
scenes.image_prompt: a grand dimensional hourglass in warm amber and gold, every falling sand grain is a tiny glowing photograph memory, drifting golden bokeh, premium nostalgic-mystical art, dark warm background, no text

scenes.text: And your brain doesn't record evenly. It's not a security camera. It's a highlights editor.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The editor at the desk, cutting for highlights.
scenes.query: film editor cutting reels at desk warm lamp vintage

scenes.text: Its rule is simple: NEW gets footage. Repeat gets skipped.
scenes.semantic_anchor: PREMIUM GRAPHIC: two conveyor film strips - one blazing with colorful full frames, one gray and nearly empty, a brass gate sorting moments between them.
scenes.image_prompt: two dimensional film strip conveyors side by side in warm light, one blazing with rich colorful glowing frames, the other pale gray with sparse faded frames, an ornate brass sorting gate directing glowing moments between them, premium machinery art, no text

scenes.text: When you were nine, everything was new. First thunderstorm you really watched. First betrayal. First perfect pop song.
scenes.semantic_anchor: First storm, fully recorded.
scenes.query: child watching lightning storm through window awe

scenes.text: Every day shipped a full reel to the archive. Dense footage. So when you look back... that summer is MILES long.
scenes.semantic_anchor: An attic bursting with the reels of one childhood summer.
scenes.query: overflowing boxes of photographs and film reels attic warm

scenes.text: Now look at last Tuesday. Same commute. Same lunch. Same scroll. Same shows.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The gray loop of the repeated day.
scenes.query: crowd commuting gray station routine timelapse

scenes.text: Your editor glanced at it and said: got it already. Skip.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Stamped and skipped: the unrecorded day.
scenes.query: rubber stamp hitting paper rapidly office desk

scenes.text: A whole year of repeats can compress into a highlight reel twenty minutes long. THAT'S where the years go.
scenes.semantic_anchor: PREMIUM GRAPHIC: a vast amber archive where childhood years stand as thick glowing volumes and adult years shrink to thin gray slivers on the shelf.
scenes.image_prompt: a grand dimensional archive shelf in warm amber light where early volumes are thick massive glowing golden books and later volumes shrink into thin pale gray slivers, cinematic perspective, premium nostalgic library art, no text

scenes.text: They didn't speed up. They just stopped being recorded.
scenes.semantic_anchor: A camera pointed at nothing worth saving.
scenes.query: security camera in empty gray hallway static

scenes.text: And it gets deeper. In the moment, boredom feels slow. But in memory, it's instant — because there's nothing to replay.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Slow to live, instant to remember: the boredom paradox.
scenes.query: person waiting bored at bus stop gray day

scenes.text: Terror is the reverse. People who fall from heights report time stretching like taffy. Their editor panic-records EVERYTHING.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The panic-recording of a fall: time stretched by density.
scenes.query: skydiver falling through clouds pov dramatic

scenes.text: Scientists tested it: memory in fear runs so dense that seconds swell into small eternities... in the replay.
scenes.semantic_anchor: A shattering second, swollen with recorded detail.
scenes.query: slow motion glass shattering light refracting

scenes.text: So hold the equation. Novelty writes footage. Footage builds length. Length is how long your life FEELS.
scenes.semantic_anchor: PREMIUM GRAPHIC: a glowing golden equation of light - a spark flowing into film frames flowing into a long radiant timeline, pure visual grammar.
scenes.image_prompt: an elegant dimensional flow diagram of pure light: a golden spark flowing into glowing film frames flowing into a long radiant expanding timeline river, warm amber and gold, premium abstract schematic, absolutely no letters or numbers

scenes.text: Which flips everything. The length of your life, as lived from the inside, is not measured in years.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The wrong measuring tape for a life.
scenes.query: tape measure being pulled out slowly close up warm

scenes.text: It's measured in FIRSTS.
scenes.semantic_anchor: A first step: the true unit of lived time.
scenes.query: child taking first steps toward parent golden light

scenes.text: And firsts are the one resource you can manufacture. For free. On purpose.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Planting a first by hand.
scenes.query: hands planting seedling in soil morning light

scenes.text: A new street home. A food you can't pronounce. A conversation with the neighbor you've nodded at for six years.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The six-year nod, finally becoming a conversation.
scenes.query: two neighbors talking over fence laughing warm evening

scenes.text: Each one forces the editor to roll film. Each one makes this year LONGER — not on the calendar. In you.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The editor forced to roll: length being written.
scenes.query: film reel spinning projector warm light close

scenes.text: You can't slow time. Nobody can. But you can record more of it.
scenes.semantic_anchor: PREMIUM GRAPHIC: a small figure walking into a horizon that unrolls as blank glowing film frames filling with color at each step, seasons shifting hues along the strip.
scenes.image_prompt: a small silhouetted figure walking toward a horizon that unrolls as a road of blank glowing film frames, each frame filling with vivid color as the figure passes, the strip shifting through seasonal palettes spring green summer gold autumn red winter blue, premium cinematic metaphor, no text

scenes.text: So do one thing tomorrow you have never done. Anything. Make it small. Make it strange.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The unfamiliar door, opened on purpose.
scenes.query: person opening unfamiliar door curious warm light

scenes.text: ...That's one extra frame you just bought. ...Roll film.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The projector starts: a life given one more frame.
scenes.query: old film projector starting up beam cutting darkness
